title: Our time here on Earth is short, and yet there's many games we want but can't experience. For years I've been unable to find games that fit many of my tastes cause they're too niche, nobody wants what I want, they all ridicule the ideas. I hope AI can let us make our own games easily in the future.
author: Present-Chocolate-24
selftext:
Perhaps if AI gets good enough in a decade or so, we'll be able to generate any games we want. Even those of us with no talent and bad ideas that everyone hates lol.  
  
For example, here's a game I have a craving for. A hardcore simulation where everything costs money, you have a lot of needs, money isn't that easy to make. And it's an urban open world sort of like GTA. But there's a lot more simulation and survival elements than GTA, money takes more effort to make and also every single little thing costs money. But the gameplay loop would balance it so it's not too tedious, the satisfaction would be to eventually overcome the grind through various upgrades.

replies.author: Present-Chocolate-24
replies.body:
In my opinion, yes and no. It'd be buggy and not quite what you want. Especially since with every new prompt to edit things to make them more like what you want, there'll be more and more room for bugs.

Not to mention the cost would be insane rn.

Maybe in 5-10 years.

comments.author: toroidalvoid
comments.body:
Your idea is totally doable.

Grand Theft Accounting.

What's the first job or way to make money you have in mind?

replies.author: Present-Chocolate-24
replies.body:
Glad you asked! Before I get to the actual job, I want to mention that it'd start paying quite little. Later in the game you'll make more but for now we start relatively slow, progression is part of the fun.

Naturally, if we keep the player poor for too long and upgrades are too expensive, it becomes boring.

So we'd have to have upgrades that really speed things up, something to look forward to. It'd be so satisfying when you buy an upgrade and now your income is almost doubled.

The balance here is finnicky, gotta make the game last a while, a short game won't do. But you don't wanna bore the player either. Quite tricky. Incremental games are a good inspiration for this, but they tend to be too fast. They're games meant to be played for a few hours, whereas this game would ideally be an experience  that lasts a few dozen hours.

Anyway, onto the jobs themselves.

I don't think the jobs really matter, it's not really about that.

It's more of a game about progression systems, upgrades. 

So you've got several progression systems, many upgrades you can work towards. And yet the survival systems and everything requiring money slows you down a bit. Every upgrade feels great cause it makes survival and paying for stuff easier.

Actually, the other comment was right, I'm not sure what I want. I don't know how to balance this to make it fun. Sounds like it'd either be too tedious or too easy from the upgrades.

replies.author: toroidalvoid
replies.body: What Claude plan are you on? You probably have enough of an idea to get started

comments.author: Cultural-Basket-8576
comments.body:
As a game dev of 10 years, I have the unfortunate news for you that the only person who never gets to experience the game as a player is the person who made it.

Your viewpoint into the game is so warped due to the creation and iteration process that you can never just play the game.

So you need to hope that someone else makes your dream game!
